creatures: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production transparent pixel-art monster animation atlas for an original commercial-quality creature-collecting RPG. Create ONE exact 5-column by 4-row sprite sheet, all twenty cells equally sized and aligned, generous transparent gutters, no text or borders. Every column a different original creature, all facing three-quarter toward the viewer's right, full body visible, feet at the same baseline per row, consistent scale: column 1 a brave fluffy-eared feline adventurer with flame-shaped cheek tufts and an amber scarf clasp; column 2 a lean long-eared wolfdog with flowing wind tufts and curled bushy tail; column 3 a stocky mouse beast with enormous round ears, faceted stone shoulder pads and sturdy paws; column 4 a low lizard dragon with branching leaf antlers, fern dorsal fins and long curled tail; column 5 an elegant coiled moon serpent with crescent crown fins, segmented belly and long whiskers. All primary fur/skin is desaturated turquoise blue (for runtime palette swapping), warm ivory bellies/muzzles, navy ink shadows, small gold and coral accents, ivory eye highlights. Row 1: neutral idle poses. Row 2: walking stride left foot forward / snake stretched. Row 3: opposite walking stride right foot forward / snake coil compressed. Row 4: striking spellcasting battle poses with raised limb/head and a tiny bright accent, no large effects. Match anatomy, details, markings and proportions exactly within each column across all rows. Visual quality target: exquisite 96-pixel monster sprites with deliberate crisp pixel clusters, expressive eyes, confident angular silhouettes, three-tone material shading, selective dark outlines and warm rim highlights, comparable to polished indie monster RPGs like Cassette Beasts and modern high-end 2D pixel art. These are original designs, not existing game characters. NOT smooth vector shapes, NOT plush toy 3D renders, NOT blurry painted pixels. Orthographic RPG view slightly from above, consistent upper-left sunlight. Canvas landscape 5:4 ratio, ideal 1600 by 1280. Uniform grid cell centers x=10%,30%,50%,70%,90%; y=12.5%,37.5%,62.5%,87.5%. Each creature occupies at most 75% of its cell width and 78% of height including the serpentine tail, no sprite touches another cell. Truly transparent alpha background.

props: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: reusable scenery sprites for an original premium pixel-art RPG. ONE atlas with exactly 16 separated objects, aligned in a precise 4 columns by 4 rows grid. Each object is entirely contained in its square cell with at least 12% transparent margins; no labels, no borders, no ground plane. Orthographic three-quarter overhead top-down RPG view with fronts facing bottom, not diamond-isometric. Upper-left warm sunlight, cool blue-purple shadows, crisp pixel clusters, selective dark outlines, exquisite handcrafted sprite detail like the best modern indie pixel RPG environment art. Cohesive palette of deep pine teal, moss jade, ochre, muted coral, indigo shade. Row 1 left to right: full lush broadleaf tree with clearly visible short trunk and dense layered asymmetric leaf clusters; full tall sculptural pine tree; a leafy fern and wildflower clump; dense flowering pink shrub. Row 2: large layered granite outcrop covered in ochre lichen; a weathered ancient stone monolith carved with an unlettered spiral; a pale sandstone arch rock; two stacked wooden supply crates with copper straps. Row 3: full coconut palm tree with curved trunk and sweeping fronds; coral and shells clump; jagged dark basalt outcrop with glowing orange fissures; a squat red volcanic vent with luminous ember core. Row 4: large purple amethyst crystal cluster; pale cyan glowing crystal cluster; cluster of bioluminescent blue mushrooms; ornate brass town streetlamp with warm cream light. All whole objects including tree canopy and base visible, all consistent pixel resolution, material richness and lighting. No soft painterly texture, no flat geometric emoji shapes, no copied game assets. Square canvas, true alpha transparent background.
